title: Ten seconds of trouble, ten minutes of outage
summary: A short blip is over, but the system never recovers.

statement.situation: An internal API handles about 700 requests/s with comfortable headroom. For ten seconds a burst of extra traffic pushes it past its limit. The burst ends, yet the service stays overloaded and keeps failing for minutes. The clients — hundreds of third-party integrations you don't control — retry failed or slow calls up to three times, 100 ms apart, and time out after half a second.
symptoms: Error rate stays high long after the trigger ended
Latency is enormous for requests that do succeed
Total attempts are several times the real demand
requirements: The service must return to normal on its own shortly after the burst
Retries must not be able to sustain the overload
Don't turn away traffic that fits within capacity
constraints: The application's server accepts connections into a very deep backlog (you can't shrink it)

learningObjectives: Metastable failures: a trigger that outlives itself
Bounding queues by age, not size
Why capacity alone doesn't fix retry amplification

references.title: Google SRE book: Addressing cascading failures
AWS Builders' Library: Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter

scenarios.name: A 10-second burst
scenarios.description: Normal 700 req/s. For 10 s at t=20 the load rises to 1,600 req/s. Clients time out after 500 ms.

successCriteria.label: Back to ≥ 98% success within 40 s of the burst ending
Normal traffic is served normally afterwards (p99 ≤ 300 ms)
